referents.why: 'you' (2ms) refusing, inside Yahweh's message, which is addressed to Pharaoh.
referents.category: second person inside a quoted speech

referents.why: 'I' striking: the speaker of the message, Yahweh, named as the LORD in the verse before.
referents.category: first person inside a divine speech

referents.why: 'your' territory: second person masculine singular, Pharaoh.

links.why: 'refuse ... to let them go': an infinitive completing a verb of refusing is its object, not a purpose.
links.category: infinitive after refuse read as purpose

links.why: the infinitive is the object of refusing: a clause nested in a role of the clause.
direction reversed: the condition is cl0 and what it conditions is the next consequence clause cl2.
the waw of 'but if' introduces a condition, not a plain and.
a Hebrew condition precedes what it governs: 'behold, I strike' is the consequence of 'if you refuse'.
waw joins the 'behold' clause to the striking clause; both are one consequence.

groups.why: the condition 'you refuse' and its consequence; cl3 is carried by the and link from cl2.
